name: Acetaminophen
category: Pain Reliever , Fever Reducer
description: Acetaminophen is used to reduce fever and relieve mild to moderate pain, including headaches, toothaches, muscle aches, back pain, and menstrual cramps. It can also help relieve pain caused by colds and the flu. Unlike some other pain relievers, such as Ibuprofen, acetaminophen does not reduce swelling or inflammation.
considerations: Liver safety: Taking too much acetaminophen can cause serious liver damage, even if you initially feel well. Seek immediate medical advice or contact a poison centre if an overdose is suspected.
Other medications: Do not combine it with other medicines containing acetaminophen, including many cold and flu products.
Alcohol and existing conditions: Ask your doctor before use if you have liver or kidney disease or regularly drink three or more alcoholic drinks daily.
Medication interactions: Consult your doctor or pharmacist before taking acetaminophen if you use warfarin, a blood-thinning medication.
Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Consult a healthcare professional and use the lowest effective dose for the shortest necessary time.

description: Simvastatin helps lower LDL (“bad”) cholesterol. It may reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke in people who need it. It is usually taken regularly for long-term benefit.
considerations: Seek advice promptly for unexplained muscle pain, weakness or dark urine.
Many medicines can interact; some require avoiding simvastatin or lowering its dose.
Ask about avoiding grapefruit products, which may increase medicine levels.
Discuss liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding with your clinician.
Do not increase the dose yourself and keep up with cholesterol follow-up.

fdaWarnings: Rare but serious reactions: Serious muscle breakdown, especially with interacting drugs or high doses. Liver injury. Important precautions: Seek advice promptly for unexplained muscle pain, weakness or dark urine. Many medicines can interact; some require avoiding simvastatin or lowering its dose. Ask about avoiding grapefruit products, which may increase medicine levels. Discuss liver disease, pregnancy or breastfeeding with your clinician. Do not increase the dose yourself and keep up with cholesterol follow-up.
fdaDosage: Available strengths / formulation: Oral tablets commonly 10 mg, 20 mg, 40 mg and 80 mg; high-dose 80 mg use is very restricted. Usual adult dosing: Usually taken once daily in the evening, at the prescribed dose. Maximum daily dose: 40 mg daily is a common adult upper maintenance dose; 80 mg carries extra muscle risk and is restricted to specific existing users. Individual interaction limits can be much lower.
